body:
This is about the replacement of `'` with `’` as the supposedly correct character, right?

Looking at [Wikipedia Apostrophe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostrophe) and specifically [the section typographic form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostrophe#Typographic_form), it seems that both are useable and correct; where `’` is the explicit apostrophe, and `'` is a generalized character that can be used for an apostrophe amongst other meanings/symbol generalization.

> With the invention of the [typewriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typewriter), a "neutral" or "straight" shape quotation mark, ', was created to represent a number of different glyphs with a single keystroke: the apostrophe, both the opening and the closing single [quotation marks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quotation_mark), the single [primes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_(symbol)), and on some typewriters even the [exclamation point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclamation_point) (by backspacing and overprinting with a period). This is known as the typewriter apostrophe or 'vertical apostrophe'.

_It seems I was misled a bit about only one being explicitly, typographically correctness, as [that is the case in German](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostroph#Typografisch_korrekt)._

I think there would still be value in using an apostrophe over the typewriter apostrophe for differentiation to the code single quote - but it is somewhat questionable to do so only in this document and not everywhere leading to inconsistencies, and when it is not explicitly incorrect to use either. And when one, presumably, sees `'` in en texts more often.

Shall I remove the apostrophe change commit form this PR?

 By convention, most modules have a prefix of default terminal color (e.g. `via` in "nodejs") and an empty space as a suffix.
 
+### Strings
+
+In TOML syntax, [text values](https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0#string) are declared with `'`, `"`, `'''`, or `"""`.
+
+The following Starship syntax symbols have special usage in a format string and must be escaped to display as that character: `$ [ ] ( )`.
+
+| Symbol | Type                      | Notes         |
+| ------ | ------------------------- | ------------- |
+| `'`    | literal string            | recommended   |
+| `"`    | string                    | more escaping |
+| `'''`  | multi-line literal string |               |
+| `"""`  | multi-line string         |               |
+
+For example:
+
+```toml
+# literal string (recommended)
+format = '☺\☻ '
+
+# regular string
+format = "☺\\☻ "
+
+# escaping Starship symbols
+format = '\[\$\] '
+```
+
+When using line breaks, multi-line declarations can be used.
+For example, if you want to print a `$` symbol on a new line, the following values for `format` are equivalent:
+
+```toml
+# with literal string (recommended)
+format = '''
+
+\$'''
body: I feel like `"""` should be preferred over `'''`.  Using a construction like in the [`$all` explanation](https://starship.rs/config/#default-prompt-format) seems to be somewhat popular among users.
